newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's citrus exports seen down in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's citrus exports seen down in 96/97.

text.p: Morocco's citrus exports will at best reach 520,000 tonnes in the 1996-97 season from 625,000 tonnes in 1995-96, a spokesman for Morocco's citrus association said on Wednesday.
He said the season, which closes in mid-June, should produce total exports "somewhere between 512,000 tonnes up to 520,000"
The spokesman attributed the fall to heavy rains which had cut output and had also favoured pests which had impaired the quality of the crop.
There had also been reduced demand in Europe, the main market for the North African country's citrus harvest.
Exports in the year to 25 May 1997 had reached 503,666 tonnes from 589,333 tonnes in the same period last year, he added.
The country's main fruit and citrus farming areas are located in the southern and northern areas of Souss and Gharb respectively.
